title: India rejects Nepal’s objection to Kailash Mansarovar Yatra through Lipulekh pass, calls it unjustified - News On AIR
description: India rejects Nepal’s objection to Kailash Mansarovar Yatra through Lipulekh pass, calls it unjustified  News On AIR
publisher.title: News On AIR
full_article:
India has rejected Nepal’s claim over Lipulekh Pass, termed it as a long-standing route for the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra since 1954 and the Yatra through this route has been going on for decades. Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal in a social media post said this in response to claims related to border issues made by Foreign Ministry of Nepal in the context of the annual Kailash Manasarovar Yatra.

He stressed that India’s position in this regard had been consistent and clear and this is not a new development. Mr Jaiswal pointed out that India has consistently maintained that such claims are neither justified nor based on historical facts and evidence. He stressed that such unilateral artificial enlargement of territorial claims is untenable. The spokesperson added that India remains open to a constructive interaction with Nepal on all issues in the bilateral relationship, including on resolving agreed outstanding boundary issues through dialogue and diplomacy.

title: Nepal approves IN Groupe for new 10M-record biometric ID system - Biometric Update
description: Nepal approves IN Groupe for new 10M-record biometric ID system  Biometric Update
publisher.title: Biometric Update
full_article:
Nepalese authorities have selected French identity firm IN Groupe for a new Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) with a capacity of 10 million biometric records through a government-to-government arrangement. The company has been a partner of the French government for more than five centuries.

The announcement comes as the license of the current ABIS in use is said to be nearing expiry with capacity left for just a few thousand data entries.

The Kathmandu Post reports that the process is a direct procurement that bypassed normal tender procedures, which is allowed by the country’s Public Procurement Act. The decision was approved by cabinet last month following recommendations of the Department of National Identity and Civil Registration.

The procurement is meant to secure the necessary software and hardware license to maintain and upgrade the capacity of Nepal’s national biometric infrastructure, which is critical for issuing national ID cards, passports, and managing voter registration.

“The price of the ABIS system will be finalized after the negotiation team concludes discussions and reaches an agreement. We have already communicated our decision to the company,” Krishna Poudel, director general of the department, is quoted as saying. The new procurement rate per record processed is the same as what Nepal paid for in 2019.

According to the Post, the existing ABIS license for the Nepal national ID card (NID) was originally supplied by Safran Identity & Security, whose identity documents business later became part of IDEMIA Smart Identity, acquired by IN Groupe last year. Idemia had been a long-standing partner of the Nepalese government for biometric passports, until two German firms took over the contract last year in a move that has been trailed by complaints about alleged procurement irregularities.

Nepal’s new ABIS procurement comes as the country is intensifying efforts to expand and modernize its identity infrastructure which it considers the backbone of its digital transformation drive. It is integrating the ID into a growing number of use cases, including a plan to make the credential acceptable for cross-border travel with India. The country has faced criticisms over huge loans incurred by the government for digital infrastructure projects.

A tender for Nepal’s National Identity Card Management Information System (NIDMIS) was cancelled in May with information that authorities had opted to handle the job internally.

title: China’s grouse compels CTA withdrawal from upcoming Tibetan studies int’l conference in Nepal - Tibetan Review
description: China’s grouse compels CTA withdrawal from upcoming Tibetan studies int’l conference in Nepal  Tibetan Review
publisher.title: Tibetan Review
full_article:
(TibetanReview.net, Jul27’26) – It has now emerged that China’s concern about the 17th International Association for Tibetan Studies (IATS) Conference to be held in Nepal’s capital Kathmandu over Aug 23-29 was on the planned participation of researchers from the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA) think tank, the Tibet Policy Institute (TPI), in their official capacity, according to an english.nepalnews.com commentary Jul 26 and an indiatoday.in report Jul 27.

The very name “CTA” is taboo to the ears of the Communist Chinese leaders, who deride it as a part of what they call the “Dalai (Lama) separatist clique”. This is despite the fact that the Dalai Lama, Tibet’s exiled spiritual leader, and the CTA only seek genuine autonomy for their Tibetan homeland, not independence.

China views any form of official recognition of the Dalai Lama or the CTA, or any criticism of the human rights situation in Tibet as challenge to its claim of sovereignty over Tibet.

The commentary cited a senior security official as saying that on Jul 21 China’s Ambassador to Nepal, Mr Zhang Maoming, met with Nepali Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai and expressed concerns about the conference after learning that some CTA representatives were expected to participate officially.

The reports quoted the source as saying: “The ambassador did not ask for the conference to be cancelled, but expressed concern that it could become a platform for anti-China rhetoric. Perhaps to avoid placing additional pressure on the Nepalese government and to ensure the conference proceeds smoothly, the CTA decided not to send its official representatives.”

The reports also quoted a second security official as saying: “Respecting Nepal’s foreign policy and to avoid creating an uncomfortable situation, the CTA decided at its Jul 21 meeting in Dharamshala not to participate officially. However, it has indicated that Tibetan scholars and experts may still attend the conference as private individuals.”

And so, while the CTA has decided not to participate officially, its scholars who have already registered may still attend the conference in their personal capacity.

However, the organisers’ preliminary registration list reportedly no longer carries some of the five named CTA researchers, though it still includes other individuals connected to the administration, among them at least one representative associated with the CTA, said the english.nepalnews.com commentary.

It said Beijing’s pressure has already forced the Dalai Lama’s exile administration to withdraw formal participation, turning a scholarly conference into a fresh test of Kathmandu’s balancing act between China and the West.

It said what should have been a routine academic activity has instead become entangled in diplomatic pressure, with China’s ambassador securing a formal Tibetan exile pullback even before the seminar opens.

The distinction between an institutional pullback and an ongoing informal individual presence is the most significant new detail in the story as the seminar’s opening date nears, and it shows Beijing’s diplomatic pressure achieving a concrete outcome even without any written protest or public demand, the commentary said.

* * *

Interestingly, around 100 participants from China are expected to attend the conference. The big question is whether they will use it as a platform to air China’s propaganda on Tibet. China has the second-largest representation, the report cited the organisers as saying.

The researchers will come from Lhasa, Sichuan, Qinghai, and Beijing, as well as from Harvard University, Columbia University, the University of Oxford, and the University of Cambridge, are expected to participate.

In addition, representatives from the China Tibetology Research Center, along with delegates from Buddhist monasteries in India, Taiwan, and Japan, are also set to attend the conference in Kathmandu.

* * *

The IATS Seminar is the flagship gathering of an international scholarly body built entirely around Tibetan studies, a field covering Tibetan Buddhism, linguistics, history, art, medicine, law and the everyday life of Tibetan communities scattered across the Himalayas and beyond. The participants include scholars, university professors, historians, linguists, theologians, and sociologists specialising in Tibetan studies.

More than 700 delegates from 39 countries have registered, with the United States contributing the largest delegation of about 150 participants.

Established in 1979 at the University of Oxford, its primary objective is to promote research related to Tibet. The seminar rotates host cities roughly once every three years.

This is the first time the IATS Conference is being held in Nepal, with its previous Asian venues being Japan (1989) and Mongolia (2013). The local co-organisers are Kathmandu University’s Himalayan Centre for Asian Studies (HiCAS) and the Centre for Buddhist Studies, which is associated with the Rangjung Yeshe Institute. The conferene is held every few years.

The conference is being coordinated by Dr Sagar Sharma, Director, Himalayan Centre for Asian Studies (HiCAS), Kathmandu University, and Rangjung Yeshe Institute’s Thomas Doctor.

Dr Sharma has said all preparations were being carried out in coordination with the government and security agencies.

“Hosting such a major international conference in Kathmandu is an achievement in itself. Since this is purely an academic event, there should be no problems,” he has said.

(TibetanReview.net, Jul27’26) – अब॑ ई बात सामने ऐलऽ छै कि नेपाल केरऽ राजधानी काठमांडू म॑ २३-२९ अगस्त क॑ होबै वाला १७वां इंटरनेशनल एसोसिएशन फॉर तिब्बती स्टडीज (आईएटीएस) सम्मेलन के बारे म॑ चीन केरऽ चिंता केंद्रीय तिब्बती प्रशासन (सीटीए) केरऽ थिंक टैंक, तिब्बत नीति संस्थान (टीपीआई) केरऽ शोधकर्ता सिनी के अपनऽ आधिकारिक क्षमता म॑ योजनाबद्ध भागीदारी प॑ छेलै एकटा english.nepalnews.com कमेंट्री 26 जुलाई आ एकटा indiatoday.in रिपोर्ट 27 जुलाई।

“सीटीए” नाम ही साम्यवादी चीनी नेता के कान में वर्जित छै, जे एकरऽ उपहास करै छै कि वू “दलाई (लामा) अलगाववादी गुट” के हिस्सा के रूप में कहै छै । ई बात के बावजूद छै कि तिब्बत केरऽ निर्वासित आध्यात्मिक नेता दलाई लामा आरू सीटीए खाली अपनऽ तिब्बती मातृभूमि लेली वास्तविक स्वायत्तता के तलाश करै छै, आजादी नै ।

चीन दलाई लामा या सीटीए क॑ कोनो भी तरह के आधिकारिक मान्यता, या तिब्बत म॑ मानव अधिकारऽ के स्थिति के कोनो भी आलोचना क॑ तिब्बत प॑ ओकरऽ संप्रभुता के दावा क॑ चुनौती के रूप म॑ देखै छै ।

टिप्पणी म॑ सुरक्षा केरऽ एगो वरिष्ठ अधिकारी के हवाला स॑ कहलऽ गेलऽ छै कि २१ जुलाई क॑ नेपाल म॑ चीन केरऽ राजदूत श्री झांग माओमिंग न॑ नेपाली विदेश सचिव अमृत बहादुर राय स॑ भेंट करी क॑ ई जानला के बाद सम्मेलन के बारे म॑ चिंता व्यक्त करलकै कि कुछ सीटीए प्रतिनिधि सिनी के आधिकारिक तौर प॑ भाग लेबै के उम्मीद छै ।

रिपोर्ट में सूत्र के हवाला स कहल गेल अछि जे, “राजदूत सम्मेलन के रद्द करय लेल नै कहलखिन, मुदा चिंता व्यक्त केलनि जे ई चीन विरोधी बयानबाजी के मंच बनि सकैत अछि।शायद नेपाल सरकार पर अतिरिक्त दबाव बनेबा स बचय लेल आ सम्मेलन के सुचारू रूप स आगू बढ़ब सुनिश्चित करय लेल सीटीए अपन आधिकारिक प्रतिनिधि के नहि भेजबाक फैसला केलक।”

रिपोर्ट सब में एकटा दोसर सुरक्षा अधिकारी के हवाला स सेहो कहल गेल अछि जे, “नेपाल के विदेश नीति के सम्मान करैत आ असहज स्थिति नै पैदा करय लेल सीटीए 21 जुलाई के धर्मशाला में बैसार में आधिकारिक तौर पर भाग नै लेबय के फैसला केलक अछि।मुदा संकेत देलक अछि जे तिब्बती विद्वान आ विशेषज्ञ एखनो निजी व्यक्ति के रूप में सम्मेलन में उपस्थित भ सकैत छथि।”

आरू ई लेली सीटीए न॑ आधिकारिक तौर प॑ भाग नै लेबै के फैसला करी लेल॑ छै, लेकिन ओकरऽ विद्वान जे पहिने स॑ ही पंजीकरण करी चुकलऽ छै, वू अखनी भी अपनऽ व्यक्तिगत क्षमता म॑ सम्मेलन म॑ भाग ल॑ सकै छै ।

लेकिन खबर छै कि आयोजकऽ के प्रारंभिक पंजीकरण सूची म॑ अब॑ सीटीए केरऽ नामित पांच शोधकर्ता म॑ स॑ कुछ नै छै, हालांकि एकरा म॑ अखनी भी प्रशासन स॑ जुड़लऽ अन्य व्यक्ति भी शामिल छै, जेकरा म॑ सीटीए स॑ जुड़लऽ कम स॑ कम एगो प्रतिनिधि भी शामिल छै, english.nepalnews.com केरऽ टिप्पणी म॑ कहलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

ओकरा म॑ कहलऽ गेलऽ छै कि बीजिंग केरऽ दबाव के वजह स॑ दलाई लामा केरऽ निर्वासित प्रशासन क॑ औपचारिक भागीदारी वापस लेबै ल॑ मजबूर होय गेलऽ छै, जेकरा स॑ एगो विद्वान सम्मेलन क॑ चीन आरू पश्चिम के बीच काठमांडू केरऽ संतुलन बनाबै के काम केरऽ एगो नया परीक्षा म॑ बदली देलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

ओकरा म॑ कहलऽ गेलऽ छै कि जे नियमित शैक्षणिक गतिविधि होना चाहियऽ छेलै, वू एकरऽ बदला म॑ कूटनीतिक दबाव म॑ उलझलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ चीन केरऽ राजदूत न॑ सेमिनार खुलै स॑ पहल॑ ही औपचारिक तिब्बती निर्वासन पुलबैक सुरक्षित करी लेल॑ छै ।

टिप्पणी म॑ कहलऽ गेलऽ छै कि संस्थागत पुलबैक आरू जारी अनौपचारिक व्यक्तिगत उपस्थिति के बीच के अंतर कहानी म॑ सबसें महत्वपूर्ण नया विवरण छै, कैन्हेंकि गोष्ठी केरऽ उद्घाटन के तारीख नजदीक आबी रहलऽ छै, आरू ई दर्शाबै छै कि बीजिंग केरऽ कूटनीतिक दबाव क॑ बिना कोनो लिखित विरोध या जन मांग के भी ठोस परिणाम हासिल करलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

* * *

मजेदार बात ई छै कि चीन स॑ लगभग १०० प्रतिभागी केरऽ ई सम्मेलन म॑ भाग लेबै के उम्मीद छै । बड़का सवाल ई छै कि की हुनी एकरा चीन केरऽ प्रचार तिब्बत प॑ प्रसारित करै लेली एगो मंच के रूप म॑ इस्तेमाल करतै । रिपोर्ट म॑ आयोजकऽ के हवाला स॑ कहलऽ गेलऽ छै कि चीन केरऽ प्रतिनिधित्व दोसरऽ सबसें बड़ऽ छै ।

शोधकर्ता ल्हासा, सिचुआन, किंघाई, आरू बीजिंग के साथ-साथ हार्वर्ड विश्वविद्यालय, कोलंबिया विश्वविद्यालय, ऑक्सफोर्ड विश्वविद्यालय, आरू कैम्ब्रिज विश्वविद्यालय स॑ भी ऐतै, जेकरा म॑ भाग लेबै के उम्मीद छै ।

एकरऽ अलावा चीन तिब्बत विज्ञान अनुसंधान केंद्र केरऽ प्रतिनिधि सिनी के साथ-साथ भारत, ताइवान, आरू जापान केरऽ बौद्ध मठऽ के प्रतिनिधि सिनी भी काठमांडू म॑ आयोजित ई सम्मेलन म॑ भाग लेबै वाला छै ।

* * *

आईएटीएस सेमिनार पूर्ण रूप स॑ तिब्बती अध्ययन के आसपास बनलऽ एगो अंतर्राष्ट्रीय विद्वानऽ के निकाय केरऽ प्रमुख सभा छेकै, जेकरा म॑ तिब्बती बौद्ध धर्म, भाषा विज्ञान, इतिहास, कला, चिकित्सा, कानून आरू हिमालय आरू ओकरा स॑ बाहर बिखरी गेलऽ तिब्बती समुदायऽ के रोजमर्रा के जीवन शामिल छै । प्रतिभागी म॑ विद्वान, विश्वविद्यालय के प्रोफेसर, इतिहासकार, भाषाविद, धर्मशास्त्री, आरू तिब्बती अध्ययन म॑ विशेषज्ञता रखै वाला समाजशास्त्री शामिल छै ।

३९ देशऽ स॑ ७०० स॑ भी अधिक प्रतिनिधि न॑ पंजीकरण करी लेल॑ छै, जेकरा म॑ अमेरिका न॑ लगभग १५० प्रतिभागी केरऽ सबस॑ बड़ऽ प्रतिनिधिमंडल के योगदान देल॑ छै ।

ऑक्सफोर्ड विश्वविद्यालय म॑ १९७९ म॑ स्थापित एकरऽ प्राथमिक उद्देश्य तिब्बत स॑ जुड़लऽ शोध क॑ बढ़ावा देना छै । ई गोष्ठी मोटा-मोटी हर तीन साल मे एक बेर मेजबान शहर कए घुमाबैत अछि।

सम्मेलन के संयोजन काठमांडू विश्वविद्यालय के हिमालयन सेंटर फॉर एशियन स्टडीज (हाइसीएएस) के निदेशक डॉ. सागर शर्मा आ रंगजंग येशे संस्थान के थॉमस डॉक्टर क रहल छथिन्ह.

ओ कहलनि जे, काठमांडू मे एहन पैघ अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सम्मेलन के आयोजन अपने आप मे एकटा उपलब्धि अछि, चूँकि ई विशुद्ध रूप स शैक्षणिक आयोजन अछि, ताहि लेल कोनो समस्या नहि हेबाक चाही।

While collecting mushrooms in a community forest in Nepal, local forest users came across the unusual sight of a rare king cobra nest.

The discovery stands out for two reasons: King cobras are considered vulnerable, and they are the only snakes known to build nests.

What happened?

According to The Rising Nepal, community forest chairman Bhandari said community forest users found the nest on July 15 near Jhakri Sota in the Ambe Community Forest of Ghorahi Sub-Metropolitan City-18 while they were searching for mushrooms.

Bhandari said the site was secured after the nest was found with help from snake rescuer and conservationist Kuldeep Neupane, who has been involved in snake rescue and conservation work in the area for the past four years.

Since the discovery, access to the nesting site has been limited, and local residents have been stopped from collecting grass, firewood, and mushrooms in the surrounding area.

Om Bahadur Oli, acting chief of the Division Forest Office in Dang, said officials are watching the area more closely and coordinating with the community forest users' committee to keep it protected. Neupane has also continued to inspect the nest regularly.

Snake researcher and conservationist Basanta Subedi said female king cobras make nests from dry leaves and other vegetation, then remain with them until the eggs hatch.

A female king cobra generally lays 30 to 40 eggs, which hatch in two to three months. The species can grow longer than 18 feet (5.5 meters) and is recognized as the world's longest venomous snake.

Why does it matter?

By feeding on both venomous and nonvenomous snakes, king cobras help support ecological balance.

Subedi said that if king cobra populations fall, other venomous snakes could become more common, potentially leading to more snakebite cases.

The discovery highlights the growing overlap between people and wildlife. In this case, people searching for food in a community forest came upon a nesting site in an area also used to collect grass and firewood.

A king cobra nest near a frequently used forest area can be dangerous if people unknowingly get too close, especially when a female is guarding eggs.

Subedi also said that Nepal protects pythons but does not list king cobras among the country's protected species despite their vulnerable status.

What's being done?

The immediate response has focused on giving the nest space.

The Division Forest Office has increased monitoring of the area and is working with the local forest users' committee to protect it.

The office also keeps venomous snakes that rescuers remove from places near human settlements for conservation.

Neupane said he has rescued and conserved around 3,000 venomous and nonvenomous snakes in the area.

Kathmandu. The Nepal Medical Association has announced a halt to all services except emergencies in hospitals across the country today (Tuesday) in protest of the heinous attack on doctors and health workers at Narayani Hospital in Birgunj and the mistreatment at the District Administration Office, Parsa.

Issuing a press release on Monday, the association informed that all services except emergencies in government, non-governmental, and private hospitals across the country would be shut down on Tuesday, August 1, 2023.

Narayani Hospital Demands Action Based on CCTV Footage

According to the association, on July 25, 2023, Dr. Pramod Ram and other doctors and health workers at Narayani Hospital were subjected to a heinous attack, resulting in serious head injuries, and the hospital was vandalized.

Committee Formed to Investigate Narayani Hospital Incident

While negotiations were underway at the District Administration Office, Parsa, demanding legal action against the perpetrators of the same incident, the association has strongly condemned the incident, stating that the police chief used force in the presence of the Chief District Officer (CDO) to verbally abuse and mistreat central executive committee members of the association and the president of the Narayani branch, among other doctors.

Narayani Hospital Incident: Ministry Determined to Create a Working Environment for Doctors

The Nepal Medical Association has demanded the immediate arrest of those who carried out the heinous attack on Dr. Pramod Ram and other health workers and strict action against them under the 'Health Workers and Health Institutions Protection Act, 2066 (First Amendment, 2079)'. Furthermore, the association has demanded that the state take immediate action against the Chief District Officer and Police Chief of Parsa involved in the insult and mistreatment of doctors during the negotiation.

Nepal Medical Association Announces to Close OPDs Across the Country Tomorrow Committee Formed to Investigate Narayani Hospital Incident In protest of the state's oppressive behavior, emergency services have been symbolically shut down today, and further protest programs will be decided by a general meeting to be held today. The press release, signed by the association's General Secretary Dr. Bishwaraj Dawadi and President Dr. Badri Rijal, apologizes for the inconvenience caused to patients by this movement and clarifies that the entire responsibility for this must be borne by the Government of Nepal itself. title: Nepali Congress Demands Release of Two Farmers Detained in India - Ratopati
description: Nepali Congress Demands Release of Two Farmers Detained in India  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. Nepali Congress has demanded the government to immediately release two Nepali farmers who were arrested while going to India for chemical fertilizer and are currently in Indian jail.

Congress General Secretary Pradip Poudel, issuing a press release, drew the government's attention to take diplomatic and legal initiatives for the release of two farmers from Sarlaahi's Balara Municipality, Suresh Prasad Singh and Nagendra Prasad Singh.

When chemical fertilizer was not available in Nepal on time, they were arrested by Indian security forces while bringing 2 bags of Urea and DAP fertilizer from the border Indian market Sonbarsa out of compulsion. They have been in Dumra jail in Sitamarhi, Bihar for the past 20 days.

Congress has stated that it is unfortunate that farmers who went to get fertilizer for their own fields have been arrested and kept in jail for 20 days. "It is extremely ironic that fertilizer is in the warehouse and farmers are in jail," the statement said.

Congress has criticized the government, stating that farmers are directly bearing the brunt of weaknesses in fertilizer supply management, lack of planning, and administrative incompetence. The statement said, "By not being able to provide chemical fertilizer on time and in sufficient quantity, our farmer अन्नदाता have been forced to suffer hardship during the farming season for years."

Nepali Congress has urged not to consider the farmers as smugglers as they had gone to collect fertilizer for their own farming and not for any commercial gain. Congress has also requested the Indian government, keeping in mind the historical friendship between Nepal and India, the open border, and the intimate relationship at the public level, to release the arrested farmers and provide necessary legal facilitation.

title: Dr. KC ends hunger strike after 7-point deal with govt - The Rising Nepal
description: Dr. KC ends hunger strike after 7-point deal with govt  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
By Raman Poudel, Kathmandu, July 28 : Dr. Govinda KC ended his hunger strike on Monday evening after reaching a seven-point agreement with the government, bringing to a close his protest demanding reforms in medical education, healthcare, and good governance.Dr. KC broke his fast at Seti Hospital by drinking juice offered by Chakra Bahadur Dhami, a patient’s caregiver from Bajhang, following the conclusion of negotiations between government and Dr. KC.

According to Pawan Thapa, a member of Dr. KC's negotiation team, the talks with the government reached a fruitful conclusion. Minister for Education and Sports Sasmit Pokharel himself had coordinated and collaborated with Dr. KC from the beginning to address his demands and negotiate.

The agreement's first clause commits the government to operating a teaching hospital with a minimum capacity of 300 beds at Shaheed Dashrath Chand University of Health Sciences in Kailali.

The university will immediately begin the process of establishing the hospital at full capacity and making arrangements to run MBBS and other academic programmes.

The Ministry of Health and Food Safety and the Ministry of Education and Sports will provide the necessary coordination, facilitation, and manpower required for the initiative. The government has also agreed to submit a proposal within three months to amend university-related legislation, including the Geta Act, 2082. The proposed amendments will address the qualifications and appointment process of university officials and will be tabled during the current session of the Federal Parliament.

In accordance with the agreement, the Medical Education Commission will determine student enrollment quotas based on the provisions of the National Medical Education Act, 2075, the National Medical Education Regulations, 2077, and the Integrated Procedure for Quality Assessment and Seat Determination of Educational Institutions Providing Medical Education, 2083.

The Ministry of Education has further committed to proposing the formation of a high-level task force to study the implementation of Section 47 of the National Medical Education Act, which requires medical education institutions operating in Nepal to function as non-profit and service-oriented organizations. The task force will submit its report, along with recommendations, within six months.

Through the negotiation, the government also agreed to improve access to basic services in the Far West and border regions. The government has pledged to expand healthcare, education, transportation, and employment infrastructure to reduce the dependence of local residents on neighbouring areas for essential services.

The government also expressed its commitment to take legal action and investigation against killings, arson, looting and destruction during the Gen Z movement. It has also pledged to pursue impartial investigations into corruption allegedly involving high-ranking politicians and government officials from 2046 BS to the present.

To monitor progress, both sides agreed to establish a separate task force to review the implementation status of previous agreements reached with Dr. KC. The task force will submit its findings within three months.

Thapa informed that the agreement was signed by Dr. Govinda KC on behalf of the protesting side and representing the government were Chudamani Paudel, Secretary at the Ministry of Education and Sports, Dr. Bikash Devkota, Secretary at the Ministry of Health and Food Safety, Chandrakanta Bhusal, Joint Secretary at the Ministry of Education, MP Pukar Bam, and Dr. Jagadish Prasad Agrawal, Health Advisor to the Prime Minister.

स्वास्थ्य आ खाद्य सुरक्षा मंत्रालय आ शिक्षा आ खेल मंत्रालय पहल कें लेल आवश्यक आवश्यक समन्वय, सुविधा, आ जनशक्ति प्रदान करतय. सरकार गेटा अधिनियम, 2082 सहित विश्वविद्यालय स संबंधित कानून मे संशोधन क प्रस्ताव तीन मास क भीतर पेश करबा पर सेहो सहमत भेल अछि।प्रस्तावित संशोधन मे विश्वविद्यालय क अधिकारी क योग्यता आ नियुक्ति प्रक्रिया कए संबोधित कैल जाएत आ संघीय संसद क चालू सत्र क दौरान पेश कैल जाएत।

समझौता कें अनुसार चिकित्सा शिक्षा आयोग राष्ट्रीय चिकित्सा शिक्षा अधिनियम, 2075, राष्ट्रीय चिकित्सा शिक्षा नियमावली, 2077, आ चिकित्सा शिक्षा प्रदान करय वाला शैक्षिक संस्थानक कें गुणवत्ता आकलन आ सीट निर्धारण कें लेल एकीकृत प्रक्रिया, 2083 कें प्रावधानक कें आधार पर छात्रक कें नामांकन कोटा निर्धारित करतय.

शिक्षा मन्त्रालय आगू राष्ट्रिय चिकित्सा शिक्षा अधिनियमके धारा ४७के कार्यान्वयनके अध्ययनके लेल उच्चस्तरीय कार्यदल गठनके प्रस्ताव देबाके प्रतिबद्ध भेल अछि, जाहिमे नेपालमे संचालित चिकित्सा शिक्षा संस्थानके गैर-लाभकारी आ सेवा उन्मुख संस्थाके रुपमे कार्य करबाक आवश्यकता अछि । टास्क फोर्स छह मासक भीतर सिफारिशक संग अपन रिपोर्ट जमा करत।

वार्ता के माध्यम स॑ सरकार सुदूर पश्चिम आरू सीमावर्ती क्षेत्रऽ म॑ बुनियादी सेवा के पहुँच म॑ सुधार लेली भी सहमत होय गेलै । सरकार स्वास्थ्य सेवा, शिक्षा, परिवहन, आ रोजगार बुनियादी ढाँचा कें विस्तार करय कें वादा करलक छै, ताकि स्थानीय निवासीक कें आवश्यक सेवाक कें लेल पड़ोसी क्षेत्रक पर निर्भरता कम भ सकय.

सरकार जेन जेड आन्दोलन के दौरान हत्या, आगजनी, लूटपाट आ तबाही के खिलाफ कानूनी कार्रवाई आ जांच के प्रतिबद्धता सेहो व्यक्त केलक अछि। संगहि 2046 बीएस स एखन धरि कथित तौर पर उच्च पदस्थ राजनेता आ सरकारी अधिकारी स जुड़ल भ्रष्टाचार क निष्पक्ष जांच करबाक वादा सेहो केलक अछि।

प्रगति के निगरानी के लेल दुनु पक्ष डॉ. केसी के संग भेल पूर्व समझौता के कार्यान्वयन के स्थिति के समीक्षा करय लेल अलग टास्क फोर्स के स्थापना पर सहमत भेल। टास्क फोर्स तीन मासक भीतर अपन निष्कर्ष जमा करत।

थापा न॑ जानकारी देल॑ छै कि प्रदर्शनकारी पक्ष के तरफ स॑ डॉ. गोविन्द केसी के हस्ताक्षर करलऽ गेलऽ छै आरू सरकार के प्रतिनिधित्व करै वाला शिक्षा आरू खेल मन्त्रालय के सचिव चूडामणि पौडेल, स्वास्थ्य आरू खाद्य सुरक्षा मन्त्रालय के सचिव डॉ. विकास देवकोटा, शिक्षा मंत्रालय के संयुक्त सचिव चंद्रकांत भुसाल, सांसद पुकर बम, आरू स्वास्थ्य सलाहकार डॉ. जगदीश प्रसाद अग्रवाल छेलै प्रधानमंत्री के।

title: Opinion | Nepal’s exam leak is about much more than one WhatsApp group - The Kathmandu Post
description: Opinion | Nepal’s exam leak is about much more than one WhatsApp group  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
The integrity of higher education in Nepal faced a digital betrayal on Friday. Within five minutes of the commencement of the Tribhuvan University’s Master of Business Studies (MBS) first-semester examination for ‘Organisational Behaviour’, the question paper was circulating on a WhatsApp group. A teacher known online as ‘Sulav Sir’, later identified as Sandip Singh, shared the paper and subsequently provided a 16-page handwritten solution while the test was still underway. This brazen act of academic fraud allowed at least 35 active members in a group of over 1,000 to discuss answers in real-time.

Friday’s paper leak is not an isolated case but rather a symptom of a recurring and systemic issue that has plagued Nepal for decades. From the Secondary Education Examination leaks in 2019 to the cancelled MBBS entrance exams in 2014, the history of examination compromises in Nepal is a long and shameful record.

The leak of an examination paper is a blow to the entire student community. For thousands of candidates, these examinations are the culmination of years of study and financial sacrifice by their families. A paper leak shatters the mental health of students by causing stress and anxiety. In many cases, the sudden loss of a fair opportunity drives students toward clinical depression. Families also suffer financial losses from money spent on examination fees, coaching and travel. Honest students lose their motivation to study.

In this context, the response from Education Minister Sasmit Pokharel has been a welcome departure from the usual administrative inertia. He ordered the Nepal Police leadership to conduct a swift, round-the-clock investigation. This rapid coordination led to the arrest of five suspects by the Central Investigation Bureau (CIB) within 24 hours of the incident. Only one remains in custody now. Such swift action is rare in Nepal, where masterminds of past academic rackets have often avoided investigation.

Nepal can draw critical lessons from the recent chaos in neighbouring India. Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned following weeks of mass youth demonstrations organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) after the NEET-UG 2026 medical entrance exam was compromised. The Indian government’s initial hesitation and delay in taking high-level accountability only served to fuel public fury and destroy trust in national testing bodies. Nepal must avoid this trajectory by maintaining absolute transparency. The university must establish a clear policy on what constitutes a compromising threshold for an examination.

The current demand for immediate resignation of Minister Pokharel is illogical. Political figures, such as UML leader Mahesh Basnet, are calling for the Minister to step down by citing the moral precedent set in India. This demand is misplaced. Unlike the situation in India where the government hesitated, Pokharel has driven a crackdown on the perpetrators. Preliminary findings indicate that the leak was carried out by a private teacher, not an internal employee of Tribhuvan University. A minister should not be forced out because of the rogue actions of an individual outside the university’s direct payroll. Basnet is simply trying to politicise a serious academic crisis for partisan gain.

For now, the government must set a good precedent by going to the root of this incident. Swift action must be taken not just against individuals but against the structural flaws that allow these leaks to recur. Growing commercialisation of education is a primary driver of these scandals. Many institutions now care more about artificially inflating results than they do about the quality of their students. Political patronage has often protected these academic syndicates in the past, leading to a culture of impunity.

The government must ensure that digital security of examination halls becomes a priority. This includes enforcing absolute bans on personal smart devices in examination halls and utilising signal jamming. The current investigation by the CIB must be fast-tracked to ensure that perpetrators face immediate legal consequences. Nepal needs a system that treats academic merit as sacred. Only by addressing the root causes and ignoring political theatre can the university regain its credibility.

एकटा परीक्षा पत्र लीक भेला स पूरा छात्र समुदाय पर झटका लागल अछि। हजारों अभ्यर्थी के लेल ई परीक्षा परिवार के सालों के पढ़ाई आ आर्थिक बलिदान के पराकाष्ठा अछि. पेपर लीक तनाव आ चिंता पैदा क छात्र क मानसिक स्वास्थ्य कए चकनाचूर क दैत अछि। बहुत मामला मे, एकटा उचित अवसर कें अचानक नुकसान छात्रक कें नैदानिक ​​अवसाद कें तरफ ल जायत छै. परीक्षा फीस, कोचिंग आ यात्रा पर खर्च भेल पाइ स परिवार कए आर्थिक नुकसान सेहो होइत अछि। ईमानदार विद्यार्थी पढ़ाई के प्रेरणा खो दैत छथिन्ह.

एहि क्रम मे शिक्षा मंत्री सस्मित पोखरेल क प्रतिक्रिया सामान्य प्रशासनिक जड़ता स स्वागत योग्य विचलन रहल अछि। ओ नेपाल प्रहरी नेतृत्व केँ त्वरित, चौबीसों घंटा जांच करबाक आदेश देलनि। एहि तेजी सं समन्वय के कारण केंद्रीय जांच ब्यूरो (सीआईबी) घटना के 24 घंटा के भीतर पांच संदिग्ध के गिरफ्तार क लेलक। आब एकटा मात्र हिरासत मे अछि। नेपाल मे एहन त्वरित कार्रवाई दुर्लभ अछि, जतय पिछला शैक्षणिक रैकेट क मास्टरमाइंड अक्सर जांच स बचैत रहलाह अछि।

पड़ोसी देश भारत मे हाल मे भेल अराजकता स नेपाल महत्वपूर्ण सबक ल सकैत अछि। कोकरोच जनता पार्टी (सीजेपी) द्वारा NEET-UG 2026 मेडिकल एंट्री परीक्षा मे समझौता भेलाक बाद सप्ताह भरि द्वारा आयोजित युवा प्रदर्शनक बाद केंद्रीय शिक्षा मंत्री धर्मेन्द्र प्रधान इस्तीफा द देलनि। भारत सरकार केरऽ शुरुआती संकोच आरू उच्च स्तरीय जवाबदेही लेबै म॑ देरी न॑ खाली जन आक्रोश क॑ बढ़ाबै के काम करलकै आरू राष्ट्रीय परीक्षण निकाय प॑ विश्वास क॑ नष्ट करी देलकै । नेपाल के निरपेक्ष पारदर्शिता बना क एहि प्रक्षेपवक्र स बचबाक चाही। विश्वविद्यालय कें एकटा स्पष्ट नीति स्थापित करनाय होयत छै की कोनों परीक्षा कें लेल समझौता कें सीमा की छै.

मंत्री पोखरेल के तत्काल इस्तीफा के वर्तमान मांग तर्कहीन अछि. एमाले नेता महेश बस्नेत सन राजनीतिक हस्ती भारत मे बनल नैतिक मिसाल के हवाला दैत मंत्री के पद छोड़य के आह्वान क रहल छथिन्ह. ई मांग गलत जगह पर अछि। भारत केरऽ जे स्थिति सरकार संकोच करलकै, ओकरा विपरीत पोखरेल न॑ अपराधी प॑ दबाव डाललकै । प्रारंभिक निष्कर्ष बताबै छै कि ई लीक त्रिभुवन विश्वविद्यालय केरऽ आंतरिक कर्मचारी नै, बल्कि निजी शिक्षक न॑ करलकै । विश्वविद्यालय के डायरेक्ट पेरोल सं बाहर कोनो व्यक्ति के बदमाश काज के कारण कोनो मंत्री के जबरदस्ती बाहर नहिं निकालल जेबाक चाही. बस्नेट बस पक्षपातपूर्ण लाभ के लेल गंभीर शैक्षणिक संकट के राजनीतिकरण करय के कोशिश क रहल छथिन्ह.

फिलहाल सरकार के एहि घटना के जड़ि मे जा क नीक मिसाल कायम करय पड़त. खाली व्यक्ति के खिलाफ ही नै बल्कि संरचनात्मक खामी के खिलाफ भी तेजी स॑ कार्रवाई करना जरूरी छै जेकरा स॑ ई लीक दोबारा होय जाय छै । शिक्षा के बढ़ैत व्यावसायिकरण एहि घोटाला के प्राथमिक चालक अछि. आब बहुत संस्थान के अपन छात्र के गुणवत्ता सं बेसि कृत्रिम रूप सं रिजल्ट फुलाबय के चिंता अछि. राजनीतिक संरक्षण न॑ अक्सर ई शैक्षणिक सिंडिकेशनऽ क॑ पूर्व म॑ भी सुरक्षा देल॑ छै, जेकरा स॑ दंडहीनता के संस्कृति पैदा होय गेलऽ छै ।

सरकार के ई सुनिश्चित करय पड़त जे परीक्षा हॉल के डिजिटल सुरक्षा प्राथमिकता मे बनय. एहि मे परीक्षा हॉल मे पर्सनल स्मार्ट डिवाइस पर पूर्ण प्रतिबंध लागू करब आ सिग्नल जामिंग क उपयोग शामिल अछि। सीआईबी द्वारा वर्तमान जांच कए तेजी स करबाक चाही ताकि इ सुनिश्चित कैल जा सकए जे अपराधी कए तत्काल कानूनी परिणाम क सामना करय पड़य। नेपाल के एहन व्यवस्था चाही जे शैक्षणिक योग्यता के पवित्र मानय. मूल कारण के संबोधित क राजनीतिक रंगमंच के अनदेखी केला स मात्र विश्वविद्यालय अपन विश्वसनीयता वापस पाबि सकैत अछि।

full_article:
Stretching from Nagdhunga in Kathmandu to Sisnekhola in Dhading, Nagdhunga Surungmarga (Nagdhunga Tunnel Road), the first tunnel road of its kind, is expected to ease traffic congestion, reduce travel time, improve road safety and give a boost to economic activity and tourism. This section of road, a gateway to Kathmandu, witnesses traffic jams throughout the year. The inauguration of much-awaited tunnel road marks the modernisation of road infrastructure in Nepal. The successful completion of this project is expected to give momentum to similar national pride projects that are under construction in different parts of the country.





Built with around Rs. 21.5 billion in concessional loans from the Japanese government and Rs. 6 billion from the Nepal government, the tunnel bears international standard, with a modern ventilation system, emergency exits, fire protection equipment, and surveillance cameras. The main tunnel that stretches 2.7 kilometres includes a parallel escape tunnel to enhance safety. The tunnel is expected to reduce travel distance by 8 kilometres and travel time by 30 to 40 minutes.





During its construction phase, the tunnel provided employment opportunities to engineers, technicians and locals. It has offered valuable knowledge in tunnel engineering and advanced construction techniques, which can be replicated in other projects in Nepal, as tunnel roads are suitable for many mountainous terrains in Nepal. Kathmandu depends on supplies from other parts of Nepal, and during natural calamities and other extreme conditions, the supply chain in Kathmandu often gets disrupted. After the completion of the tunnel, Kathmandu won't have to go through this situation. Likewise, the tunnel would make travel to western Nepal more convenient; better connectivity is expected to boost tourism.





During the construction of the tunnel that lasted around seven years, the road connecting to the capital city got further damaged and was hardly repaired, adding to travel woes. People experience 3- 4 hours long jam during major festivals. The tunnel is expected to handle around 8,000 vehicles a day once it reaches full capacity. If that traffic volume is achieved, it is projected to generate around Rs. 350 million in annual toll revenue. Although the project was originally scheduled for completion by April 26, 2023, construction was hampered by delays on the part of the contractor, the COVID-19 pandemic, and local obstructions. The construction period for the project—for which the contract was signed on November 14, 2019—was most recently extended until October 25, 2025.





On Monday, the tunnel was jointly inaugurated by Minister for Infrastructure Development Sunil Lamsal, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Japan to Nepal Toru Maeda and Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) President Akihiko Tanaka. Minister Lamsal noted that the successful completion of the Nagdhunga Tunnel marked the beginning of a new era in Nepal's transport infrastructure. He said that more tunnels would be constructed across the country. While the inauguration of the tunnel deserves applause, a single infrastructure like this cannot transform the economy of the country. It needs more modern road infrastructure like this. At the same time, we cannot deny the fact that this tunnel alone cannot solve the issue of traffic congestion in the Nagdhunga area. For a long-term solution, our highways need to be upgraded in a timely manner. Nagdhunga-Sisneri tunnel should be the beginning, not the end, of the modernisation of Nepal's road infrastructure.

लगभग 1000 रुपया के साथ निर्मित। जापान सरकार स 21.5 अरब रियायती ऋण आ 10 लाख टका कर्ज। नेपाल सरकारसँ ६ अरब रुपैयाँक ई सुरंग अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मानक धारण करैत अछि, जाहिमे आधुनिक वेंटिलेशन सिस्टम, आपातकालीन निकास, अग्नि सुरक्षा उपकरण, आ निगरानी कैमरा अछि । 2.7 किलोमीटर तक फैलल मुख्य सुरंग मे सुरक्षा बढ़ेबा लेल समानांतर एस्केप सुरंग सेहो शामिल अछि। एहि सुरंग स यात्रा क दूरी 8 किलोमीटर आ यात्रा क समय मे 30 स 40 मिनट क कमी हेबाक उम्मीद अछि।

full_article:
Nepal has formally requested India to recognize its National Identity Card as a valid travel document for Nepali citizens entering the country. If approved, the National Identity Card would become the third accepted travel document alongside passports and citizenship certificates. The proposal, submitted through diplomatic channels, aims to simplify air and land travel between the two neighboring countries. Nepali authorities say the move could make cross-border movement more convenient for travelers while strengthening people-to-people connectivity.

full_article:
“If a city is designed for children, it will work for women, the elderly, and everyone else.”

This profound concept served as the central theme of the third Urban Bootcamp, organised by the Cities 4 Women (C4W) project in Nepal. As our valleys and plains rapidly urbanise, the bootcamp provided a much-needed platform for architects, urban planners, and local leaders to share practical approaches to designing child-friendly, inclusive, and climate-resilient public spaces. The event started with the mayor of Sunwal Municipality, Bimala Aryal, talking about how Sunwal became a "Child-friendly Municipality".

The Ministry for Women, Children and Social Welfare awarded Sunwal with the designation after it completed the minimum index of child-friendly governance related to child protection, child development, child participation, child survival and organisational development. The municipality became successful in achieving the title as it had strictly carried out works by formulating a code of conduct to complete the minimum index determined by the Child-Friendly Local Governance Implementation Work Procedure as per the Child-Friendly Local Governance National Strategy-2068 BS.

Working with children

“When a municipality invests in children, they will grow up and do well in the country and around the world,” the mayor said. Following that, the Urban Planner, Prabal Dahal at UN-Habitat, presented on the importance of designing with children. “By 2050, 70 per cent of the world’s children will live in cities; therefore, they should be the focus because they will be the ones living in the cities,” he highlighted.

The presentation on SDG localisation emphasised the need for working with children rather than for them. And that collaborative approach can only be achieved through empathy and inclusivity. For example, Imukhel Children’s Park, an initiative supported by UNICEF, delivered a multi-functional space that serves as a playground, a performance area, and even a safe haven during emergencies by directly consulting with children, older adults, and persons with disabilities.

Similarly, Anupama Nalleri of Save the Children International challenged the "one-size-fits-all" mentality that often plagues city planning and advocated for a nuanced approach to public spaces. Children of different ages interact with public spaces differently. A toddler's needs might not match those of a teenager. Recognising that a toddler's need for safety is fundamentally different from an adolescent's need for freedom allows urban designers to move beyond generic playgrounds towards a more inclusive civic fabric.

Ultimately, designing for the specific developmental needs of childhood ensures that cities do more than house children; they help them grow into healthy, connected adults. Following through with regional experiences, Professor Bharat Dahiya of Thammasat University in Thailand, reflected on the challenges of building child-friendly cities in the Asia-Pacific region.

To ground the discussion in everyday experience, he shared a conversation he had with his 14-year-old daughter before leaving for the conference. He had asked her a simple question: “What makes a city good?" "More plants and trees," she answered, emphasising that children learn best about nature by experiencing it directly rather than only through textbooks. She also highlighted the importance of smooth, accessible sidewalks, safe bike lanes, and cities that feel secure from crime.

The response reminded the audience that listening to children often reveals the most fundamental qualities of a livable city. Several Nepali practitioners also echoed this message by sharing their work. Niharika Mathema from Digo Bikas Institute presented on “Placemaking through Play,” emphasising that the city itself should function as a public space. She explained the three stages of placemaking-place taking, place making, and place keeping and shared examples such as Car-Free Saturdays in Hadigaun, where streets temporarily transform into vibrant social spaces for play and community interaction.

She also introduced the concept of “Playbourhoods,” which aims to reactivate neighbourhood-based play through tactical urbanism, sensory walks, and heritage treasure hunts. Similarly, Ruchi Khakurel presented on the present conditions of child play areas in Kathmandu and how they can be made more child-friendly through some small interventions. Likewise, Rubin Shrestha from Cycle Society Nepal gave a brief update on the project that they are doing in various parts of the valley, which includes proposing more cycle-friendly routes in different parts of Lalitpur Municipality.

The representative from Lets Play presented on “Understanding the Complexity of Play in the Public Spaces of the Core Area of Patan, Nepal,” which was completely based on the research that they carried out in Patan. Anna Koskinen from the University of Turku, Finland, presented on “Lessons from the Field: Spain and Finland”. Likewise, Nilima Thapa Shrestha and Barsha Shrestha presented the public spaces designs that Cities 4 Women project is designing at the moment, keeping children, women and persons with disabilities in mind.

Urban planning

Building child-friendly cities in Nepal requires prioritising children’s needs in everyday urban planning. Children's participation must be formally embedded in municipal planning through schools, child clubs, and participatory design processes, supported by dedicated budgets that endure beyond political cycles. Child-friendly principles should be integrated into local plans, street design standards, building bylaws, and public space guidelines so that every new intervention contributes to safer and more inclusive cities.

Tactical urbanism, such as play streets, car-free days, and pop-up parks, can serve as a practical testing ground for piloting ideas, learning quickly, and scaling successful solutions. At the same time, underutilised public land should be reclaimed to expand access to safe play and social spaces, particularly in dense urban neighbourhoods. Achieving this depends on strengthened local capacity and long-term partnerships among governments, communities, civil society, and the private sector. We need to embed empathy into the way we plan, design, and build our urban infrastructure. Above all, we need to listen to children.

(Thapaliya is an architect and urban designer.)
translated:
“कोनो शहर जँ बच्चा सभक लेल बनाओल गेल हो तँ ओ महिला, बुजुर्ग, आ सभ गोटेक लेल काज करत।”

ई गहन अवधारणा नेपाल मे सिटीज ४ महिला (सी ४ डब्लू) परियोजना द्वारा आयोजित तेसर अर्बन बूटकैम्प के केन्द्रीय विषय के रूप मे काज केलक । जेना-जेना हमरऽ घाटी आरू मैदान तेजी स॑ शहरी होय जाय छै, बूटकैंप न॑ आर्किटेक्ट, शहरी योजनाकार, आरू स्थानीय नेता सिनी लेली एगो बहुत जरूरी मंच प्रदान करलकै ताकि बच्चा सिनी के अनुकूल, समावेशी, आरू जलवायु के प्रति लचीला सार्वजनिक स्थानऽ के डिजाइन करै के व्यावहारिक दृष्टिकोण साझा करलऽ जाय सक॑ । आयोजनक शुरुआत सुनवल नगरपालिकाक मेयर बिमला अर्यल द्वारा सुनवाल कोना "बाल-अनुकूल नगरपालिका" बनल ताहि पर गप्प कएल गेल ।

महिला, बाल आ समाज कल्याण मंत्रालय बाल संरक्षण, बाल विकास, बाल भागीदारी, बाल जीवित रहनाय आ संगठनात्मक विकास सं संबंधित बाल अनुकूल शासन कें न्यूनतम सूचकांक पूरा करला कें बाद सुनवाल कें इ पदनाम सं सम्मानित करलकय. बाल अनुकूल स्थानीय शासन कार्यान्वयन कार्य प्रक्रिया द्वारा निर्धारित न्यूनतम सूचकांक पूरा करबाक लेल आचार संहिता बना क सख्ती स काज केने छल नगरपालिका उपाधि प्राप्त करबा मे सफल भेल छल ।

बच्चा सभक संग काज करब

मेयर कहला जे जखन कोनो नगरपालिका बच्चा मे निवेश करत तखन ओ पैघ भ कए देश आ दुनिया भरि मे नीक काज करत। एकरऽ बाद यूएन-हैबिटैट केरऽ अर्बन प्लानर प्रबल दाहाल न॑ बच्चा सिनी के साथ डिजाइनिंग के महत्व प॑ प्रस्तुति देलकै । ओ रेखांकित केलनि जे, 2050 तक दुनिया के 70 प्रतिशत बच्चा शहर मे रहत, ताहि लेल हुनका सब पर ध्यान देबाक चाही, किया कि ओ शहर मे रहय वाला हेताह।

एसडीजी स्थानीयकरण पर प्रस्तुति मे बच्चाक कें लेल नहि बल्कि ओकरा संग काज करय कें जरूरत पर जोर देल गेलय. आरू वू सहयोगात्मक दृष्टिकोण सहानुभूति आरू समावेशीता के माध्यम स॑ ही प्राप्त करलऽ जाब॑ सकै छै । उदाहरण कें लेल, इमुखेल चिल्ड्रेन पार्क, जे यूनिसेफ कें समर्थन सं कैल गेल पहल छै, एकटा बहु-कार्यात्मक जगह उपलब्ध करौलक छै जे आपातकालीन स्थितियक कें दौरान खेल कें मैदान, प्रदर्शन क्षेत्र, आ सुरक्षित ठिकाना कें रूप मे सेहो काज करय छै, सीधा बच्चाक, वृद्ध वयस्कक, आ दिव्यांग व्यक्तियक सं परामर्श कयर.

तहिना सेव द चिल्ड्रेन इंटरनेशनल केरऽ अनुपमा नल्लेरी न॑ "एक आकार-सब लेली" मानसिकता क॑ चुनौती देलकै जे अक्सर शहर नियोजन क॑ परेशान करै छै आरू सार्वजनिक स्थानऽ प॑ सूक्ष्म दृष्टिकोण के वकालत करलकै । विभिन्न उम्र कें बच्चाक सार्वजनिक स्थानक कें साथ अलग-अलग तरह सं बातचीत करएयत छै. छोट बच्चा कें जरूरत किशोर कें जरूरत सं मेल नहि खा सकएय छै. इ स्वीकार करनाय की एकटा छोट बच्चा कें सुरक्षा कें जरूरत एकटा किशोर कें स्वतंत्रता कें जरूरत सं मौलिक रूप सं अलग छै, शहरी डिजाइनर कें जेनेरिक खेल कें मैदान सं आगू बढ़एय कें अनुमति देयत छै आ बेसि समावेशी नागरिक ताना-बाना कें तरफ बढ़एयत छै.

अंततः, बचपन कें विशिष्ट विकासात्मक जरूरतक कें लेल डिजाइन करनाय इ सुनिश्चित करएयत छै की शहरक बच्चाक कें घर करएय सं बेसि काज करएयत छै; ओ ओकरा स्वस्थ, जुड़ल वयस्कक मे बढ़एय मे मदद करएयत छै. क्षेत्रीय अनुभव के बाद थाईलैंड के थम्मसत विश्वविद्यालय के प्रोफेसर भरत दहिया न॑ एशिया-प्रशांत क्षेत्र म॑ बाल-अनुकूल शहर के निर्माण के चुनौती प॑ चिंतन करलकै ।

रोजमर्रा के अनुभव में चर्चा के ग्राउंड करय लेल ओ सम्मेलन में जेबा सं पहिने अपन 14 साल के बेटी सं भेल एकटा गप्प-सप्प साझा केलनि. ओ ओकरासँ एकटा साधारण प्रश्न पुछने छलाह : “शहरकेँ नीक की बनबैत छैक ?” "अधिक पौधा आरू गाछ" - ई बात प॑ जोर दैत॑ हुअ॑ हुनी ई बात प॑ जोर देलकै कि बच्चा सिनी प्रकृति के बारे म॑ सबसें अच्छा तरीका स॑ खाली पाठ्यपुस्तक के माध्यम स॑ नै बल्कि सीधा अनुभव करी क॑ सीखै छै । हुनी चिकनी, सुलभ फुटपाथ, सुरक्षित बाइक लेन, आरू अपराध स॑ सुरक्षित महसूस करै वाला शहर के महत्व प॑ भी प्रकाश डाललकै ।

प्रतिक्रिया दर्शक क॑ याद दिलाबै छेलै कि बच्चा सिनी के बात सुनला स॑ अक्सर रहना योग्य शहर केरऽ सबसें मौलिक गुण सामने आबै छै । कतेको नेपाली साधक सेहो अपन काज साझा करैत एहि संदेश केँ गूँजौलनि । दिगो विकास संस्थान केरऽ निहारिका मथेमा न॑ “प्लेसमेकिंग थ्रू प्ले” प॑ प्रस्तुति देलकै, जेकरा म॑ ई बात प॑ जोर देलऽ गेलै कि शहर क॑ ही एगो सार्वजनिक स्थान के रूप म॑ काम करना चाहियऽ । हुनी प्लेसमेकिंग-प्लेस टेकिंग, प्लेस मेकिंग, आरू प्लेस कीपिंग के तीन चरण के बारे म॑ बतैलकै आरू उदाहरण साझा करलकै जेना कि हडिगौन म॑ कार-फ्री सैटरडेज, जहां सड़क अस्थायी रूप स॑ खेल आरू सामुदायिक बातचीत लेली जीवंत सामाजिक स्थान म॑ बदली जाय छै ।

हुनी “प्लेबरहुड” के अवधारणा भी पेश करलकै, जेकरऽ उद्देश्य सामरिक शहरीकरण, संवेदी सैर, आरू धरोहर खजाना के खोज के माध्यम स॑ पड़ोस आधारित खेल क॑ पुनः सक्रिय करना छै । तहिना रुचि खकुरेल काठमांडू मे बाल खेल क्षेत्रक वर्तमान स्थिति आ किछु छोट-छोट हस्तक्षेपक माध्यम सँ ओकरा कोना बेसी बाल-अनुकूल बनाओल जा सकैत अछि ताहि पर प्रस्तुत केलनि । तहिना साइकल सोसाइटी नेपाल सँ रूबिन श्रेष्ठ घाटी के विभिन्न भाग मे जे परियोजना क रहल छथि ताहि पर संक्षिप्त अपडेट देलनि, जाहि मे ललितपुर नगरपालिका के विभिन्न भाग मे बेसी साइकिल अनुकूल मार्ग के प्रस्ताव सेहो शामिल अछि।

लेट्स प्ले केरऽ प्रतिनिधि न॑ “नेपाल केरऽ पाटन केरऽ कोर एरिया केरऽ पब्लिक स्पेस म॑ प्ले केरऽ जटिलता क॑ समझना” प॑ प्रस्तुति देलकै, जे पूर्ण रूप स॑ पाटन म॑ जे शोध करलकै ओकरा प॑ आधारित छेलै । फिनलैंड के तुर्कू विश्वविद्यालय के अन्ना कोस्किनेन न॑ “फील्ड स॑ सबक: स्पेन आरू फिनलैंड” प॑ प्रस्तुति देलकै । तहिना निलिमा थापा श्रेष्ठ आ बरशा श्रेष्ठ सार्वजनिक स्थानक डिजाइन प्रस्तुत केलनि जे सिटीज 4 महिला परियोजना एखन डिजाइन क रहल अछि, जाहि मे बच्चा, महिला आ दिव्यांग व्यक्ति के ध्यान मे राखल गेल अछि।

शहरी नियोजन

नेपाल मे बाल-अनुकूल शहर बनेबा मे रोजमर्रा के शहरी नियोजन मे बच्चा के जरूरत के प्राथमिकता देबय के जरूरत अछि. बच्चाक कें भागीदारी कें औपचारिक रूप सं स्कूलक, बाल क्लबक, आ सहभागिता वाला डिजाइन प्रक्रियाक कें माध्यम सं नगर निगम योजना मे समाहित कैल जेबाक चाही, जेकर समर्थन समर्पित बजटक कें द्वारा कैल जैतय जे राजनीतिक चक्रक सं परे टिकय छै. बच्चाक कें अनुकूल सिद्धांतक कें स्थानीय योजनाक, सड़क डिजाइन मानक, भवन उपनियमक, आ सार्वजनिक स्थान दिशा निर्देशक मे एकीकृत कैल जेबाक चाही ताकि हर नव हस्तक्षेप सुरक्षित आ बेसि समावेशी शहरक मे योगदान दे सकय.

सामरिक शहरीकरण, जेना कि खेल सड़क, कार-मुक्त दिन, आ पॉप-अप पार्क, विचारक कें पायलटिंग, जल्दी सीखनाय, आ सफल समाधानक कें स्केल करय कें लेल एकटा व्यावहारिक परीक्षण स्थल कें रूप मे काज कयर सकय छै. संगे-संग सुरक्षित खेल आ सामाजिक स्थानक कें पहुंच कें विस्तार कें लेल, विशेष रूप सं घना शहरी मोहल्लाक मे, कम उपयोग कैल गेल सार्वजनिक जमीनक कें पुनर्प्राप्ति कैल जेबाक चाही. एकरा प्राप्त करनाय सरकारक, समुदायक, नागरिक समाज, आ निजी क्षेत्र कें बीच स्थानीय क्षमता कें मजबूत आ दीर्घकालिक साझेदारी पर निर्भर करय छै. हमरा सब क॑ अपनऽ शहरी बुनियादी ढाँचा के योजना, डिजाइन, आरू निर्माण के तरीका म॑ सहानुभूति के समाहित करै के जरूरत छै । सबसँ ऊपर बच्चा सभक बात सुनबाक आवश्यकता अछि।

(थपलिया आर्किटेक्ट आ शहरी डिजाइनर छथि।)

KATHMANDU: Economic Digest presents a brief yet comprehensive roundup of major business developments in Nepal, delivered in clear and accessible summaries.

Nepal’s economy presented mixed signals on Monday, with strong underlying activity tempered by cautious investor sentiment and continued regulatory intervention. Despite stock market turnover surging above Rs 6.7 billion, the NEPSE index fell more than 33 points, suggesting that increased trading was driven more by selling pressure than renewed confidence.

The Nepal Rastra Bank’s decision to absorb Rs 30 billion in excess liquidity and penalize a finance company for violating reserve requirements underscores its focus on monetary discipline and financial stability. At the same time, infrastructure and policy initiatives, including the inauguration of the Nagdhunga-Sisnekhola Tunnel, progress on the Kakarbhitta-Laukahi highway, and proposed reforms to mining legislation, reflect the government’s push to improve long-term economic competitiveness.

Rising gold prices and record silver sales point to sustained demand for safe-haven assets amid market uncertainty, while the Supreme Court’s ruling on share premium reserves signals tighter corporate governance in the capital market. Positive developments in energy, with Nepal exporting surplus electricity during the monsoon, and business expansion plans by the Dairy Development Corporation, Nepal Airlines and Green Plywood Nepal indicate improving domestic economic activity.

However, unresolved cooperative fraud protests, the indefinite suspension of vehicle services in Bagmati Province and shifting labor migration patterns highlight persistent governance and structural challenges. Overall, the day’s developments portray an economy balancing reform efforts, infrastructure expansion and macroeconomic stability against fragile market confidence and institutional shortcomings.

NEPSE drops 33 points despite turnover exceeding Rs 6.7 billion

The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) index declined by 33.28 points on Monday, erasing the previous session’s gains of 7.90 points. Following the drop, the benchmark index closed at 2,701 points. The market opened on a positive note and climbed to an intraday high of 2,744 points at around 12:13 pm before reversing course and remaining in negative territory for the rest of the session. Despite the decline, trading activity increased significantly, with daily turnover rising to Rs 6.7 billion, up from Rs 4.67 billion in the previous session. Share prices of 35 companies advanced, while 235 declined and five remained unchanged.

Gold rises to Rs 288,500 per tola, silver to Rs 4,445

Gold prices in the domestic market increased again on Monday, with fine gold trading at Rs 288,500 per tola, up Rs 1,400 from the previous trading day, according to the Federation of Nepal Gold and Silver Dealers’ Association. The price of gold per 10 grams also climbed to Rs 247,340 from Rs 246,140. Silver prices rose by Rs 35 to Rs 4,445 per tola. Traders attributed the increase to movements in international precious metals prices, fluctuations in the US dollar exchange rate and changes in domestic supply and demand.

Nagdhunga tunnel inaugurated, expected to generate Rs 3.5 billion annually

The Nagdhunga-Sisnekhola Tunnel was officially inaugurated on Monday, marking the completion of Nepal’s first road tunnel project. Built at an estimated cost of Rs 29 billion, the tunnel is projected to generate around Rs 3.5 billion in annual revenue, based on an estimated daily traffic of 8,800 vehicles and a 60 percent utilization rate. The project is expected to ease congestion at Nagdhunga and improve travel between the Kathmandu Valley and the rest of the country by making journeys faster, safer and more efficient.

NRB absorbs Rs 30 billion in excess liquidity

The Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) absorbed Rs 30 billion from the banking system on Monday through a 179-day deposit collection instrument to manage excess liquidity. Class A, B and C licensed financial institutions took part in the online competitive bidding, with interest rates determined based on the lowest bids. Institutions were required to bid a minimum of Rs 100 million, while the principal and interest will be settled on January 22, 2027.

Kakarbhitta–Laukahi highway upgrade reaches 38% completion

Around 38 percent physical progress has been achieved so far in the eastern section of the Kakarbhitta–Laukahi road expansion and upgrading project being constructed along the East–West Highway. The 95-kilometer project, being implemented under the Project Directorate of the Department of Roads, has been divided into eastern and western sections. The eastern section covers the 45-kilometer stretch from Kakarbhitta to Sitapuri, where construction work has gained momentum in recent months. According to the latest project details, the combined physical progress of the first, second and third packages under the eastern section has reached 37.78 percent. Although construction has accelerated recently, only around six months remain before the current contract period expires, making an extension necessary.

Ministry finalizes bill to amend mining laws

The Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies has finalized the draft Mines and Minerals Related Laws Amendment and Integration Bill for submission to the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers under the government’s 100-day action plan. Led by Minister Gauri Kumari Yadav, the proposed legislation seeks to modernize laws governing mineral exploration, extraction, conservation and regulatory compliance. It also aims to eliminate administrative hurdles and clarify responsibilities among the federal, provincial and local governments while creating a stronger legal framework to encourage sustainable resource development and private investment.

Finance minister conducts surprise inspection of SEBON

Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle carried out an unannounced inspection of the Securities Board of Nepal (SEBON) on Monday, coinciding with a sharp decline in the secondary market, where the NEPSE index fell 33.28 points to 2,701.32. The visit comes shortly after the appointment of SEBON Chairperson Gopal Bhatta, who had been instructed by the finance minister to submit weekly progress reports on the implementation of the board’s 10-year capital market development roadmap. Investors are also closely watching regulatory developments following recent consultations between Prime Minister Balendra Shah and financial regulators, stock exchange officials and investor groups aimed at improving market confidence.

Cooperative fraud victims protest for return of deposits

Victims of cooperative fraud staged fresh protests in Kathmandu on Monday, demanding the immediate return of their savings and stronger deposit protection measures. Organized by the National Campaign for Cooperative Depositors Protection, the rally marched from Maitighar to the office of the Problematic Cooperative Management Committee in Buddhanagar and planned to continue to the National Cooperative Regulatory Authority in Pulchowk. Protesters carried copies of past government agreements and accused the government of treating small and large depositors differently. Organizers warned of more intense demonstrations if their demands remain unaddressed after the two-day awareness campaign.

DDC to open 30 new outlets in Kathmandu Valley

The Dairy Development Corporation (DDC) plans to open 30 new outlets across the Kathmandu Valley by mid-August 2026 under a new service model. According to General Manager Sharan Kumar Pandey, the new outlets will be located in areas including Budhanilkantha, Banasthali, Kalanki, Koteshwor and New Baneshwor. The corporation also reopened its renovated Basantapur outlet on Monday. In response to growing demand for products such as milk, curd, paneer and ghee, DDC also plans to expand into major cities outside the valley and launch online sales in the coming days.

Bagmati Province extends suspension of vehicle services indefinitely

The Bagmati Province government has extended the suspension of vehicle-related services indefinitely as authorities continue server upgrades and database migration needed to implement revised provincial vehicle tax rates. Although federal transport authorities had initially planned to restore services after a temporary shutdown through July 24, the provincial government said technical integration work is still underway. As a result, vehicle registration and renewal services will remain suspended until further notice.

Peak electricity demand reaches 3,248 MW

Nepal’s peak electricity demand has reached 3,248 megawatts (MW), while total daily energy consumption stands at 73,629 megawatt hours (MWh), according to the Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA). The country is not importing electricity from India at present and is instead exporting 22,102 MWh of surplus power during the monsoon season. Private hydropower producers are supplying 47,563 MWh to the national grid, while NEA subsidiaries generate 17,108 MWh and the authority’s own projects contribute 8,959 MWh. The NEA said uninterrupted electricity supply has been maintained despite continuous rainfall, with technical teams on standby to respond to any outages.

Supreme Court says share premium must remain in reserve

The Supreme Court has ruled that funds collected above the face value of shares must be kept in a dedicated reserve fund and cannot be distributed as dividends. A joint bench of Justices Manoj Kumar Sharma and Srikanta Poudel dismissed a petition seeking to cancel the initial public offering of Himalayan Reinsurance after concluding that the company had met the required financial standards. However, the court criticized the Securities Board of Nepal and the Nepal Insurance Authority for inadequate regulatory oversight and directed them to ensure that share premium funds are maintained in restricted reserves instead of being distributed as profits.

UAE becomes top destination for Nepali migrant workers

The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has overtaken Malaysia, Qatar and Saudi Arabia as the leading destination for Nepali migrant workers, driven by growing demand in the service and construction sectors after the pandemic. According to the Department of Foreign Employment’s annual report for fiscal year 2024/25, 183,580 workers received labor approval for the UAE, followed by 132,646 for Malaysia, 132,051 for Qatar and 124,583 for Saudi Arabia. The report attributes the UAE’s rise to greater availability of indoor jobs, while higher minimum wages helped sustain demand for Malaysia. Interest in Qatar and Saudi Arabia continued to decline as more Nepali workers also explored opportunities in European countries such as Romania, Croatia and Cyprus.

Nepal Airlines launches phone booking service for international flights

Nepal Airlines Corporation has introduced a telephone booking service for international flights, allowing passengers to reserve and purchase tickets by calling +977-5718538 during office hours. In addition to bookings through its sales counters, official website and mobile application, travelers can now complete the process over the phone by providing their travel details, email address, mobile number and required documents. Payments can be made using a QR code sent digitally, enabling passengers to finalize their bookings from home.

Himalayan Bullion Company’s silver sales soar to Rs 9.79 billion

Himalayan Bullion Company recorded silver sales worth Rs 9.789 billion during the first nine months of the last fiscal year, driven by rising global silver prices and increased investment demand. The figure marks a sharp rise from Rs 302 million in 2025 and Rs 474 million in 2024. Nepal’s only organized corporate silver trader improved its operating profit margin to 5.64 percent, increased shareholders’ equity to Rs 307 million and reduced its gearing ratio to 0.48, with total debt falling to less than half its equity. Supported by strong cash flows and a CARE-NP BB+ credit rating, the company imports silver from Dubai and Hong Kong.

Department warns against sale of banned goods

The Department of Commerce, Supplies and Consumer Protection has warned businesses against the illegal import, storage and sale of goods prohibited by the government. The department said import restrictions published in the Nepal Gazette on June 17, 2019, and April 6, 2020, remain in force under the Export-Import (Control) Act, 1957. It cautioned that businesses violating the rules, including those selling prohibited products through online platforms, will face legal action under the Export-Import (Control) Act, 1957, and the Consumer Protection Act, 2018.

NRB fines Reliance Finance for CRR violation

The Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) has fined Reliance Finance Rs 2,924.48 for failing to maintain the mandatory Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR). According to the central bank’s Bank Supervision Department, the Class C financial institution breached the regulatory requirement between February 22 and April 18 during the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025/26. The penalty was imposed under Section 100 of the Nepal Rastra Bank Act, 2002.

Surya Nepal posts Rs 32.36 billion annual turnover

Surya Nepal recorded a business turnover of Rs 32.356 billion in 2025, up from Rs 28.82 billion in 2024 and Rs 28.99 billion in 2023. The company maintained a strong financial position with a gearing ratio of just 0.01 and no long-term debt. It also held Rs 4.944 billion in bank deposits and more than Rs 1 billion in treasury bills at the end of the year. Established in 1986, the company is chaired by Sanjeev Puri and is owned by India’s ITC Limited (61 percent) and Nepali investors (39 percent). It manufactures cigarettes, incense sticks and packaged food products, while also exporting honey through its subsidiary, Surya Nepal Ventures.

Green Plywood Nepal plans IPO of 1.64 million shares

Green Plywood Nepal has announced plans to issue an initial public offering (IPO) of 1.64 million shares, representing 20 percent of its issued capital, after converting into a public limited company on July 15. The company has called a special general meeting for August 7 to endorse the proposal. It reported an 18.96 percent increase in sales to Rs 475 million in fiscal year 2024/25. Supported by export subsidies and steady trade with India, which accounts for 70 percent of its sales, the company increased its tangible net worth to Rs 226 million while improving its gearing ratio from 7.41 to 2.44.

Bangladesh Embassy hosts mango festival in Kathmandu

The Embassy of Bangladesh in Nepal organized the Bangladesh Mango Delicacy Exhibition and Festival in Kathmandu on Sunday to promote trade and cultural ties between the two countries. Held at Utsav Kunja Banquet, the event attracted around 250 participants, including diplomats, government officials, importers and business representatives. Visitors were introduced to popular Bangladeshi mango varieties, including Khirshapat (Himsagar), Haribhanga, Langra, Fazli, Gopalbhog and Amrapali, along with processed products such as juices, pickles, jams and jellies.

बागमती प्रदेश मे वाहन सेवा निलंबन अनिश्चित काल तक बढ़ाओल गेल अछि

सुप्रीम कोर्ट के कहनाय छनि जे शेयर प्रीमियम रिजर्व मे रहय पड़त

सुप्रीम कोर्ट के फैसला अछि जे शेयर के फेस वैल्यू सं बेसि जमा कएल गेल फंड के डेडिकेटेड रिजर्व फंड मे राखय पड़त आओर ओकरा लाभांश के रूप मे नहि बांटल जा सकैत अछि. न्यायमूर्ति मनोज कुमार शर्मा आरू श्रीकांत पौडेल केरऽ संयुक्त पीठ न॑ हिमालयन पुनर्बीमा केरऽ प्रारंभिक सार्वजनिक पेशकश क॑ रद्द करै के याचिका क॑ खारिज करी देलकै, जेकरा बाद ई निष्कर्ष निकाललऽ गेलै कि कंपनी न॑ आवश्यक वित्तीय मानक क॑ पूरा करी लेल॑ छै । लेकिन कोर्ट नेपाल के प्रतिभूति बोर्ड आरू नेपाल बीमा प्राधिकरण के अपर्याप्त नियामक निगरानी के आलोचना करतें हुअय ई सुनिश्चित करै के निर्देश देलकै कि शेयर प्रीमियम निधि क॑ लाभ के रूप म॑ वितरित करै के बजाय प्रतिबंधित भंडार म॑ रखलऽ जाय ।

नेपाल एयरलाइंस अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय उडानके लेल फोन बुकिंग सेवा शुरु केलक

सीआरआर उल्लंघन के लेल एनआरबी रिलायंस फाइनेंस पर जुर्माना लगा देलक

अनिवार्य कैश रिजर्व रेशियो (सीआरआर) निर्वाह नै करला पर नेपाल राष्ट्र बैंक रिलायंस फाइनेंस पर २,९२४.४८ रुपैया जुर्माना लगौलक अछि । केंद्रीय बैंक केरऽ बैंक पर्यवेक्षण विभाग के अनुसार, सी श्रेणी केरऽ वित्तीय संस्थान न॑ वित्तीय वर्ष 2025/26 केरऽ चारिम तिमाही के दौरान 22 फरवरी स॑ 18 अप्रैल के बीच नियामक आवश्यकता के उल्लंघन करलकै । दंड नेपाल राष्ट्र बैंक अधिनियम २००२ के धारा १०० के तहत लगाओल गेल छल ।

सूर्य नेपालमे ३२.३६ अरब रुपैयाँ वार्षिक कारोबार भेल अछि

सूर्य नेपाल मे 2025 मे 32.356 अरब टका क कारोबारी कारोबार दर्ज कैल गेल, जे 2024 मे 28.82 अरब आ 2023 मे 28.99 अरब टका छल। संगहि एहि साल क अंत मे बैंक जमा मे 4.944 अरब टका आ ट्रेजरी बिल मे एक अरब स बेसी टका छल। 1986 मे स्थापित एहि कंपनी क अध्यक्षता संजीव पुरी क रहल छथि आ एकर मालिकाना हक भारत क आईटीसी लिमिटेड (61 प्रतिशत) आ नेपाली निवेशक (39 प्रतिशत) क अछि । ई सिगरेट, धूप के छड़ी आरू पैक करलऽ खाद्य उत्पाद के निर्माण करै छै, जबकि अपनऽ सहायक कंपनी सूर्य नेपाल वेंचर्स के माध्यम स॑ शहद के निर्यात भी करै छै ।

ग्रीन प्लाईवुड नेपाल 16.4 लाख शेयर के आईपीओ के योजना बना रहल अछि

ग्रीन प्लाईवुड नेपाल 15 जुलाई कए पब्लिक लिमिटेड कंपनी मे बदललाक बाद अपन जारी पूंजी क 20 प्रतिशत क प्रतिनिधित्व करय वाला 16.4 लाख शेयर क प्रारंभिक पब्लिक ऑफरिंग (आईपीओ) जारी करबाक योजना क घोषणा केलक अछि। वित्तीय वर्ष 2024/25 मे बिक्री मे 18.96 प्रतिशत क बढ़ोतरी क संग 47.5 करोड़ टका भ गेल। निर्यात सब्सिडी आरू भारत के साथ लगातार व्यापार के समर्थन स॑ कंपनी न॑ अपनऽ मूर्त संपत्ति क॑ बढ़ा क॑ २२.६ करोड़ रुपया करी देलकै जबकि अपनऽ गियरिंग रेशियो ७.४१ स॑ बढ़ी क॑ २.४४ करी देलकै ।

बांग्लादेश दूतावास काठमाण्डौमे आम महोत्सव के आयोजन करैत अछि

नेपाल मे बांग्लादेशक दूतावास रविदिन काठमांडू मे बांग्लादेश आम स्वादिष्टता प्रदर्शनी आ महोत्सव के आयोजन केलक अछि जाहि सं दुनू देश के व्यापार आ सांस्कृतिक संबंध के बढ़ावा देल गेल अछि. उत्सव कुंजा भोज मे आयोजित एहि आयोजन मे राजनयिक, सरकारी अधिकारी, आयातकर्ता आ व्यापारिक प्रतिनिधि सहित करीब 250 प्रतिभागी शामिल छलाह। आगंतुकऽ क॑ बांग्लादेश केरऽ लोकप्रिय आम केरऽ किस्म, जेकरा म॑ खिरशपत (हिमसागर), हरिभंगा, लंगड़ा, फजली, गोपालभोग आरू आम्रपाली के साथ-साथ जूस, अचार, मुरब्बा आरू जिलेबी जैसनऽ प्रोसेस्ड उत्पाद स॑ परिचित कराय देलऽ गेलै ।
